question.text: What does the bounded corpus support about using a personal used-to-think/now reversal as an opener across text-first feeds?

selectionPolicy.description: Review every resolved opening in the current hook-frame bank that instantiates the used-to-think/now first-person belief reversal. Compare performance only within each creator file on its consistently available primary metric.
inclusionCriteria: The opening states a belief formerly held by the author.
The opening immediately replaces or destabilizes that belief.
The source resolves to a captured entry with date and metric provenance.
The fixed connective wording is grounded across at least two creator files.
exclusionCriteria: Generic contrasts that do not describe the author's changed belief.
Later-body reversals that are not part of the opening.
Rows without resolvable source provenance or a within-creator denominator.

summaries.statement: Across this bounded three-entry, two-creator sample, writers use a first-person belief reversal to establish the topic and create forward motion in the opening. Because only one of three instances is top-quartile and no controlled comparison exists, the corpus supports testing the scaffold when the source contains a real change of mind. It does not support a claim that the scaffold improves reach.
caveats: Three instances across two creators are too few for a general performance claim.
One LinkedIn result and two Substack results do not establish platform-wide behavior.
No post was tested with two alternate openings, so causal impact is unknown.

originality.note: Proposed mechanism-level scaffold only. No creator claim, example, topic, identity, or distinctive phrase is retained for generation.
originality.method: Cross-creator grounding of fixed runs of three or more words, deterministic rejection of any fixed eight-word corpus run, and manual comparison against every cited opening.
